verdict.for_whom: This is for patient players who want an immersive open-world narrative and do not mind dealing with an external launcher, but not for those who expect snappy, fast-paced action right away or want a functional online multiplayer mode.

distortion_flags.sentence: Player satisfaction is low initially due to technical setup barriers but increases drastically as players get further into the campaign.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that missions cannot be manually saved or autosaved mid-mission, requiring players to complete them in one go.

citations.review_text: There are a few great games that are ruined by their save game system. This is one of them. It treats saving games like a mother treats the cookie jar. At any point, has it saved? Can I quit? How much progress will I lose if I quit? If I'm unsure of the save status, bad game. When I play a game, I need to be able to save and quit, not be forced to finish missions in one go as some sort of purist nonsense. Giant Turd.

The controls are so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ incompetently crafted that I think anyone who made them should just be never allowed to play or work on video games again. GTA 5'S CONTROLS WERE ALREADY FINE AND WOULD HAVE WORKED PERFECTLY WHERE WITH ONLY A FEW MINOR CHANGES! DO WHAT I TELL YOU WHEN I TELL YOU! I DON'T CARE ABOUT YOUR WORTHLESS ANIMATION IF IT STOP ME FROM DOING WHAT I NEED IT TO THAT MOMENT!!!

The need for deadeye just to not immediately die is beyond incompetent game design. It's one thing for it to be an enhancement or encourage liked in GTA 5 but basically requiring me to spam it while the enemy get free aimbot just shows the level of stupidity from the devs that makes me even question if this is even the same company making the game.

So much of this game is obtuse or completely useless that I wonder why I even bother. Defusing doesn't really work when it makes sense, the difference between the core and bars for health, deadeye and stamina makes no sense. They don't even do anything but bloat the game with pointless resource management. The wanted system for just bumping into something and not even knowing what you broke or at least allowing the player to explain it was not malicious every now against just forces the player into pointless scenarios. These are just a few examples. AND WHAT'S THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ POINT OF MANUALLY SAVING IF YOU WON'T LET ME DO THAT MID LEVEL OR GIVE ME BETTER CHECKPOINTS OR EVEN LET ME CHOOSE WHEN I GET THEM?!

The story is fine enough (No where near as good as people makes it out to be, but it's vastly better then GTA 4, 5, or many other rockstar games), I like the characters, and the general environment is alright (I am very partial to Saint Dennis and the Swamp Areas). But the controls are so incompetent, the systems so annoying, and the reliance on deadeyes makes this game so pathetically crafted as a whole that I genuinely wonder if this game was specifically made to be as crap as possible to see how much the player base will tolerate …

Pretty good game. The events are pretty linear but once you get to the sandbox mode where you can pretty freely to travel in the wilderness it gets better. The single biggest problem with the game is that you cannot manually save or autosave during the missions. If your system is unstable or you cannot play until the whole mission is complete because of IRL limitations, you should avoid starting the missions which take anywhere from a couple of minutes to 30 minutes seemingly randomly. I wish the game implemented at least exit save similar to Fallout 4 survival mode which otherwise blocks saving.

The overall feel of the game is very slow and you just have to accept that because it represents the feel of the late 1890s. For a long time, pretty much nothing will happen and then out of sudden you get lots of action. If you're looking for a game where something big happens continuously, look for other games instead.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that launching the game requires using the Rockstar account launcher and third-party login or account linking can cause access blockages.

citations.review_text:
Unfortunately I cannot recommend any games from Rockstar. When I had originally signed up for an account with Rockstar, I signed up with a Comcast email that I no longer have access to and that is no longer even active. This email was linked from my Rockstar account to my Steam account. As a result, I am no longer able to play any of Rockstar's games on Steam. When you start the game, you are required to sign in through Rockstar's launcher and you have to verify your account by them sending a code to your email. I no longer have access to that email, so I am not able to verify my account. 

THERE IS ABSOLUTELY NO WORKAROUND FOR THIS

I have contacted Rockstar support multiple times to try and fix this, but they close out the support tickets saying that I am not providing enough information, or that I am not putting a ticket through the account that I no longer have access to. Rockstar does not care though, because they are such a huge company, they can afford to lose customers. I suppose they just want me to create a new Steam account and buy their games again, but I am not going to do that. I am very disappointed with Rockstar's customer service. I have bought all of their games MULTIPLE TIMES since the release of GTA III, and they cannot even help fix this small problem. All they have to do is let me link a new email to my Steam account, but they are not willing to do this.

Just be aware if you link your Rockstar account to your Steam account, you have to make sure you keep access to the email account that is linked, because otherwise you will not be able to play any of their games on Steam.

Like many here & all over Reddit; I have fallen victim to the abysmal Rockstar launcher and somehow even worse support resulting in not even being able to play any of the Rockstar games purchased via Steam including RDR2. 

My Rockstar account was seemingly hacked and 2FA methods reset. Rockstar support will actively refuse any and all proof. Literal receipts of purchased games! They will then black list you and prevent you from logging further tickets with them.  

Mid you this wasn't even to recover the account, it was to unlink it from my Steam account which would let me create a new Rockstar account to log in with. 

Nope. 

Perfectly happy to take your money and leave you high and dry. 

Avoid this publisher like the plague.
Addicted to hunting! This game honestly still has so much to do.

For 1 this playtime is incorrect. I have played 0 hours because I cannot launch the game. You are forced to use a Rockstar account to launch the game. I cannot get into this account because the MFA text with the verification code never arrives. Ive created multiple tickets with zero response and a completely unplayable game. Oh want to see your ticket? Sorry you cant access the dashboard without logging into the account you cant get into. Ridiculous and because the play time is incorrectly set to 6 hrs I sont even think I can get a refund. Not making the same mistake when GTA 6 comes out. HARD PASS

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game controls as clunky, janky, and poorly crafted.

citations.review_text:
This is a good game, but maybe overhyped. While it's clear this game is a masterpiece through its incredible and immersive world, story, characters, attention to detail, it's bogged down by clunky controls and laughably easy combat. The meat and potatoes of what you'll actually be doing in this game world is riding a horse from point a to point b. The story and cutscenes are great but each 'mission' is painfully easy thanks to deadeye, healing items, and unintelligent npc behaviours.

I really wanted to love this game but its amazing handcrafted world it's held back by lackluster gameplay.

The controls are so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ incompetently crafted that I think anyone who made them should just be never allowed to play or work on video games again. GTA 5'S CONTROLS WERE ALREADY FINE AND WOULD HAVE WORKED PERFECTLY WHERE WITH ONLY A FEW MINOR CHANGES! DO WHAT I TELL YOU WHEN I TELL YOU! I DON'T CARE ABOUT YOUR WORTHLESS ANIMATION IF IT STOP ME FROM DOING WHAT I NEED IT TO THAT MOMENT!!!

The need for deadeye just to not immediately die is beyond incompetent game design. It's one thing for it to be an enhancement or encourage liked in GTA 5 but basically requiring me to spam it while the enemy get free aimbot just shows the level of stupidity from the devs that makes me even question if this is even the same company making the game.

So much of this game is obtuse or completely useless that I wonder why I even bother. Defusing doesn't really work when it makes sense, the difference between the core and bars for health, deadeye and stamina makes no sense. They don't even do anything but bloat the game with pointless resource management. The wanted system for just bumping into something and not even knowing what you broke or at least allowing the player to explain it was not malicious every now against just forces the player into pointless scenarios. These are just a few examples. AND WHAT'S THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ POINT OF MANUALLY SAVING IF YOU WON'T LET ME DO THAT MID LEVEL OR GIVE ME BETTER CHECKPOINTS OR EVEN LET ME CHOOSE WHEN I GET THEM?!

The story is fine enough (No where near as good as people makes it out to be, but it's vastly better then GTA 4, 5, or many other rockstar games), I like the characters, and the general environment is alright (I am very partial to Saint Dennis and the Swamp Areas). But the controls are so incompetent, the systems so annoying, and the reliance on deadeyes makes this game so pathetically crafted as a whole that I genuinely wonder if this game was specifically made to be as crap as possible to see how much the player base will tolerate …

I wish I could like this game, the setting is great, the world is beautiful, and some aspects of the game are fun.

But my god are there a lot of faults. The game play is such a slog. the controls are pretty garbage and janky, the missions are repetative and the open world is just a waste. You're an outlaw with the choice of being good or a thieving bandit, great right? 
except that being a bandit is so stupid. Not only does every crime you commit, even in the middle of nowhere, get spotted by a random passerby 1000 miles away from you, they will immediately know it was you and call law enforcement with their 1900's smartphones within a few seconds.
I read that you can change your outfit and what not to really make it harder for the sherrifs to know it's you.. but so far I haven't been able to get that to work, and you'll get slapped with another 500 dollar bounty. And what did you get from your robbery? 2 dollars and maybe a tonic.

Yes I know you can cheese this by just stealing a lot with a bounty, spending all the money, and then get yourself captured, so the bounty is removed.. but that does not feel like it should be part of the gameplay, where using a cheese like this is.. supposed to be how it's meant to be played?

The gameplay is also mostly just, here is a horse, this horse is now your only companion, you will live together, and die together, there is no other way in life anymore.
Now go run across the map for an hour to do a mission that's pretty much the same as the other 10 missions. done? great now run back an hour over the empty map. Welcome back, now go another way for an hour. 

I think the only thing I somewhat enjoyed was hunting, but even there it's a slog when it's oh I just killed a high quality deer! okay now I can run with my horse for an hour again, because you can only put 1 (full) corpse on your horse. Great I get the realism here, but gameplay wise, it's a drag. 
If I wanted to repetitive things with no reward, I would just w…

So far very similar to Red Dead Redemption, further refined. The scope of the game is clearly significantly larger. However, by this time in the first game, I had already started to learn about John Marston, and I was already starting to care for him. Thusfar, I have not felt the same about Author Morgan, though I believe that I will as the story progresses. The graphics are great, some of the mechanics, like in the first game, are a bit clunky at first, but once you get used to them it's no problem. I could see the mechanics feeling better with a controller, but I have only used keyboard/mouse controls. 

So far really liking the game. I'll update this review when I complete the story.

genuinely Rockstar just HAD to ruin it with their "3rd party launcher required" a perfect 10/10 game gets nerfed because of this stupid requirement like really they could have just make us launch it and enjoy it through steam it is that simple.

claims.claim: Reviewers find the opening chapters to be slow-paced and a slog before the narrative picks up later.

citations.review_text: Yes the story feels slow at start as i never played any slow paced game , but after chapter 1 i was completely grabbed by the storyline, the characters, the soundtrack and the mechanism is really good. Playing this felt like i was Arthur Morgan  which really lead to enjoying every mission, side quests and interactions with npcs. Personally i feel like there is no game with this depth of game mechanics and gameplay wise, At last the story, what should i say just play yourself for me its 10/10 in all expectes this really taught me patience which gives reward later.

To be honest with you, i have never felt this conflicted over a Rockstar game. Like, i like the game, quite a lot honestly. It's one of my favourite games of alll time. From the storytelling, the open world, Arthur himself and the Online is tons of fun espacially if you have friends to play it with. But on the other there's some stuff I'm not particularly fond of that kinda drag the experience down for me.

To start on with, this is supposed to be a more realistic slower paced cinematic experience compared to many other Rockstar. Which isn't a bad thing. Cinematic games have existed for decades now and this one of my favourites because of how detailed it is. But there's a point where the realism is too much and many areas Rockstar put way too much focus on the Cinematics, realism and linear storytelling where it kinda drags the pacing down. The first chapters espacially are a slog to go through and it only picks up at about the second to third chapter. I guess the storytelling and amazing writing, storytelling, open world design more than makes up for it but i wished more of the focus went into the actual gameplay instead of being overly cinematic and realistic. But even so honestly, compared to many other cinematic games, it's nice to see a genuine effort to strike a good balance between gameplay and cinematics and RD2s attempt works well enough. I think Max Payne 3 and GTA 4 stricked that perfect balance between third person linear gameplay and linear storytelling and RD2 unfortunately doesn't quite stick the landing the same for me. Next, the horse. I don't have a problem with how the horse controls. Not at all, the horses here control better and more realistic than 99% of other open world games. My real problem comes with their stamina. It's ridiculous how easily it can drain. And yes, i know i can get better horse saddle but i did and that didn't fix my problem. I can't count all the times i lost a mission because my horse run out of stamina quickly throwing me…

citations.review_text:
It may sound dramatic, but I really do wonder if I will ever play something this great again. A beautiful experience in every aspect. 

Multiplayer is the only reason this game loses points. Filled with hackers/modders, and entirely abandoned by rockstar.

The single player has the GREATEST story I have ever got the luxury to play. I already wish that I can go back in time and replay it for the first time. The world is immersive and alive. I will say do NOT 100% the game like me as it does ruin a lot of the enjoyment and takes way too long and has you doing random crap. Otherwise for the average player this is a AMAZING game. +1 to games I am too afraid to replay because of the emotional damage.

Everything about RDR2 is just great, gunplay, story, graphics, ambience, open world, even just hunting and fishing is what hooked me the most and taking pictures with my trusty horse.

RDR2 offline is really fun and detailed RDR Online however is a chaotic mess where one encounter can give you an amazing time talking and enjoying with the people you're currently with and the rest of the time it's trying to survive hackers (the fun ones that just put you in the UFO or fling you across the map).

The story line is good although still has remarkable bugs. If you are into the PVP or online play including missions, well, my understanding is this game has no more maintenance. I found it very buggy, lot's of disconnects, lack of players, too many mod griefers. 
I played through the story a couple times as well as spent many hours in the online it's self at first release years ago. This does not have the same feel ONLINE, I saw no legendary creatures, fewer animals and far too many mod griefers and I could barely turn in a pelt due to the disconnects (they disappear at log out or joining a mission, dumb mechanic, imo.) It is really too bad, it was a real fun game. If you have never played the story and this is on sale at a deep discount, go for it. It is not a difficult game and is very immersive. Otherwise I would not recommend anymore. :(
Once an excellent game, now abandoned by the developer. Might as well just shut the game down. Nothing is being done to resolve grifters' and modders' issues.

Red Dead Redemption 2 is an action-adventure game developed by Rockstar Games, featuring a stunningly realistic Wild West world. Players take on the role of Arthur Morgan and experience a story filled with conflict, friendship, and sacrifice. Besides completing the main missions, players can hunt, fish, and explore a vast open world. The story is engaging, the gameplay is fun, and the graphics are outstanding. Its only drawback is the slow pace at the beginning of the game. Overall, Red Dead Redemption 2 is one of the best games ever made, offering a truly unforgettable gaming experience. 

Rating: 9.5/10

<<I'm surprised you move on two legs!>> (c)


The first hour of the tedious introduction is worth it to get into this astonishingly detailed hand-drawn world with its unprecedented simulation of wildlife and routine, meticulous physics (up to the spread of fire and wetting/soiling clothes) and a Kingpin'99-style conversation system. 

Even if you're not thrilled with the Wild West, RDR2 has a lot more to offer besides the setting. And in 2026, is still unbeaten. 
Be sure to give it a try.
